title: Poquott (Dyer's Neck)
summary: Poquott is a traditional placename for Dyer's Neck between Setauket and Port Jefferson, interpreted as clear land or open country but treated cautiously by Tooker.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Poquott / Dyer's Neck point used as a general proxy for a traditional placename; Tooker says the name is not found in early records.
history_content: The name belongs to the Setauket and Port Jefferson harbor landscape, but its early documentary basis is uncertain. Tradition and interpretation details appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as clear land or open country. A later comparison raised the possibility that the traditional form may be related to Poquossett, referring to water opening out or widening, so the interpretation needs careful review.

Why Place Names Matter

“Every place-name may convey a message about the place. Often place-names record and celebrate local and national people, events and incidents.”

— Jon Nichol, Place-names and the National Curriculum for History (2014), opening paragraph

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
whereintheworld_content: Approximate/general point on the modern Poquott / Dyer's Neck peninsula between Setauket and Port Jefferson. This marker is not an exact early-record coordinate.
